transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
My mind just won't slow down—ideas are racing all the time and I can't keep my thoughts straight anymore. It's gotten to the point where I'm having a really hard time keeping up with everything.
Have you also been experiencing periods of extreme mood swings, such as feeling very high or very low, or is it more that your thoughts are just constantly racing?

Yes, I definitely experience both. I go through stretches where I feel way up, super chatty, and easily irritated or snappy with people, but then I'll flip and feel like all the life has gone out of me, just sitting on the couch for hours. Even during those low times, my thoughts are still racing and piling on top of each other.
Can you tell me more about how long these periods of feeling 'way up' and then very low typically last, and do you notice any patterns or triggers that seem to set them off?

These high-energy phases have been going on almost constantly for the past year and a half, only easing up briefly before flaring again and leaving me feeling completely flat. It all really started when I began pushing myself so hard to become a CNA supervisor, taking on extra shifts and night classes that totally disrupted my routine.
Can you clarify if these high-energy phases and low periods occur in distinct episodes that last for days or weeks at a time, or if they can shift back and forth within the same day?

No, they aren't quick changes within the same day. These are long stretches lasting for weeks at a time where I feel completely revved up and barely sleep for days, only easing up for a little bit before starting right back up.

Can you estimate how many of these distinct high-energy and low periods you've experienced over the past year and a half, and do you recall any specific events or circumstances that seemed to trigger the switch from one phase to the other?

I'm not really sure how many distinct times it's happened because it feels like it's been going on almost constantly since I started pushing for the promotion. I also can't think of any specific triggers that cause the switch from one phase to another; it just seems to happen on its own.
Can you confirm if you have experienced at least two distinct episodes of these high-energy and low phases over the past year and a half, with each episode lasting for at least two weeks?

Yes, I've definitely had these high-energy phases flare up, ease off briefly, and then come back again multiple times over the last year and a half. They actually last much longer than just two weeks—they've been a major, persistent part of my life for most of this 17-month period, only letting up for short breaks before starting right back up.
Can you describe how your behavior and daily functioning change during these high-energy phases, such as increased activity, excessive spending, or impulsive decisions?

During those high-energy phases, I'm constantly buzzing around my apartment cleaning, reorganizing, starting new art projects, and signing up for extra shifts and classes all at once. I just can't sit still even when my body is completely exhausted, so I end up leaving tasks half-done because my mind is already jumping to the next thing. It has really impacted my ability to keep up with my charting at work and has caused me to fall behind in my classes.

Can you tell me if there have been any periods, even brief, over the past year and a half where you felt completely normal, without either the high-energy or low phases, and if so, how long those periods lasted?

To be honest, I haven't really felt completely normal at all since this started a year and a half ago, as I've spent almost the whole time either highly revved up or coming down but still feeling keyed up. There was a brief spell last winter where my mood and energy dropped back to a "so-so" level, but even then I didn't feel normal because I was still hearing whispers and felt convinced people were trying to sabotage me.
Can you confirm if you have experienced at least two distinct episodes of depression, with each episode lasting for at least two weeks, over the past year and a half?

I don't think I've had distinct, two-week-long depressive episodes like that. While I do have times where I feel flat, inactive, and lose interest in my hobbies, my main struggles have really been the high-energy phases and the racing thoughts or suspiciousness. It has never really felt like a clear episode of deep depression.

Can you clarify if, during those times when you felt flat and inactive, you experienced significant depressive symptoms such as feelings of worthlessness, guilt, or recurrent thoughts of death, which lasted for at least two weeks?

I don't recall having those specific feelings of worthlessness, guilt, or thoughts of death. Instead, my low periods have felt more like being completely flat, drained of life, and just lacking any energy to do the things I used to enjoy.

Can you describe any periods where you felt extremely happy or irritable for at least four consecutive days, and if so, did you notice any changes in your sleep patterns, energy levels, or engagement in activities during those times?

Yes, I experience those stretches frequently, feeling either way up and overexcited or extremely touchy and irritable over small things. During these times, my sleep drops to just three or four hours a night but I still wake up feeling completely wired. My energy levels skyrocket, and I find myself buzzing around cleaning, starting multiple art projects, and taking on extra shifts because I just can't sit still.

Can you confirm whether your high-energy phases and low periods have been interspersed with periods of relatively normal mood, or have they predominantly been one after the other without a return to a baseline mood in between?

I really haven't returned to my normal baseline mood for most of this time. I've spent the vast majority of the past year and a half either highly revved up or just coming down from those highs while still feeling more keyed up than my old self. The only real exception was a period during the winter where my energy and mood dropped back to a "so-so" level, but even then I didn't feel quite back to normal.

Can you specify if these episodes of high energy and low mood have occurred in a pattern that resembles a regular cycle, or have they been more sporadic and unpredictable over the past year and a half?

It doesn't really feel like a neat, predictable cycle at all. Instead, these high-energy phases have been almost constant since I started pushing for the promotion a year and a half ago, only easing up briefly before flaring right back up again. Most of the time, I've just been either completely revved up or coming down from it.

Can you confirm if the periods of high energy and the periods of feeling low have been occurring in a way that you can clearly distinguish one episode from another, or do they tend to blend together over time?

They definitely tend to blend together rather than being clearly separate. I spend most of my time either highly revved up or just coming down from those highs while still feeling more keyed up than my old normal self. The high-energy periods only ever ease up briefly before flaring right back up again.
Can you estimate the total number of months over the past year and a half where you've experienced these high-energy phases, and how many of those months were spent in a low or 'coming down' phase?

Out of the 17 months since I started pushing for the supervisor role, these high-energy phases have been going on almost the entire time. I don't really have a true 'low' phase; when I'm not fully revved up, I'm just briefly coming down but still feel more keyed up than my old self. Almost the whole year and a half has been spent in these high-energy states with only very short breaks.
Have you experienced any periods where you had at least two weeks of stable mood, without shifting into either a high-energy or low phase, over the past year and a half?

Yes, last winter I had a long spell of more than two weeks where my mood and energy dropped back to a neutral, 'so-so' level. But even though my mood felt stable then, I was still hearing those whispered voices and felt strongly that people at work were trying to sabotage me.
Can you confirm if the brief periods where you felt more stable, like last winter, lasted long enough to be considered a full remission of symptoms between episodes of high energy and low mood?

No, it definitely wasn't a full remission of all my symptoms. Even though my mood and energy leveled out to a "so-so" state last winter, I was still hearing those whispered voices and felt strongly that people at work were trying to sabotage me.

Can you confirm if the high-energy phases you've experienced over the past year and a half have lasted at least four consecutive days, and if the low phases have lasted at least two weeks, to help differentiate between the potential diagnoses?

Yes, the high-energy phases definitely last much longer than four days—they usually go on for weeks or even months at a time with very little break. I'm not really sure about "low phases" lasting two weeks, though, because my down periods feel more like flat, empty times where I just lack energy and motivation rather than a distinct period of deep depression.

Can you clarify if the high-energy phases and the periods where you feel flat or 'coming down' have distinct boundaries, or do they gradually transition into one another without clear starts and ends?

I'm not entirely sure, and it's really hard to pinpoint any exact boundaries. It feels more like I am either fully revved up or slowly sliding down from those highs, with the states blurring together rather than having a clear, sudden switch.

Can you confirm if you have experienced at least two distinct episodes of high-energy phases, with each episode lasting at least two weeks, and with at least one episode of a low phase lasting at least two weeks in between, over the past year and a half?

I know I've had those high-energy phases and times when I felt really flat, but I'm not sure if they fit that exact pattern of two-week blocks with a low phase in between. Instead, the high-energy times have been mostly constant for me, with only brief periods where things eased up and I felt "so-so" or flat.
Can you estimate how many times you've shifted from a high-energy phase to a low or 'so-so' phase and back again over the past year and a half, and roughly how long each of these cycles lasted?

I'm really not sure of the exact number of times I've shifted back and forth, or how long each of those cycles lasted. It's just that the high-energy phases have been there almost the entire time, only easing up briefly before flaring right back up again.

Can you try to approximate the average length of time you spend in a high-energy phase before you start to feel like you're coming down, and does this pattern of cycling between high-energy and lower phases seem to be getting more frequent or intense over the past year and a half?

These high-energy phases have been going on almost the entire time since I started pushing for the supervisor role a year and a half ago. They last for very long stretches and only ease up briefly before starting right back up, so I spend the vast majority of my time in this revved-up state. While I don't have an exact number of days or weeks for each phase, it feels like they have been dominant and fairly consistent throughout this whole year and a half.

Can you confirm if the periods where you felt 'so-so' or flat, like last winter, were completely free of any manic or hypomanic symptoms, or if you still experienced some level of elevated mood or energy during those times?

Yes, during that spell last winter, my mood and energy had completely dropped back to a normal, "so-so" level, and I didn't have any of those revved-up, high-energy feelings at all. But even though those manic feelings were gone, I was still hearing those whispered voices and felt convinced my coworkers were working against me.

Can you confirm if you have experienced at least two distinct episodes of high-energy phases, with each episode lasting at least two weeks, and with a clear period of normal mood or a depressive episode lasting at least two weeks in between these episodes, over the past year and a half?

I'm really not sure about the exact number of weeks or if they were distinct episodes. It mostly feels like the high-energy phases have been ongoing and dominating this past year and a half, rather than happening in clear, timed-out blocks. I've only had brief moments where things eased up or felt 'so-so' in between.

Can you clarify if the high-energy phases and low periods have occurred in a pattern that could be described as having at least two distinct episodes of abnormal mood, with each episode lasting at least two weeks, and with a period of at least two months of relatively normal mood in between these episodes, over the past year and a half?

I don't think my mood has ever gone back to normal for as long as two months. The high-energy phases have been pretty constant, only easing up briefly before starting right back up again, so there hasn't really been a long break where I felt completely normal.
Can you confirm whether you have experienced any periods lasting at least two months where you did not have either high-energy or low phases, indicating a return to a relatively normal mood?

No, I definitely haven't had any long periods like two months where my mood was back to normal. Those high-energy phases only ever ease up briefly before starting right back up again, and even during the times I'm not fully revved up, I still feel keyed up and "off" compared to my old self.

Can you confirm if there has been at least one period of at least two months where you did not experience any significant high-energy or low phases, which could indicate a period of euthymia or normal mood between episodes?

No, I haven't had any break as long as two months where I felt completely normal. These high-energy phases and feeling keyed up have been going on for almost the entire 17 months, only easing up very briefly before flaring right back up again.

Can you confirm if you have experienced at least two distinct episodes of high-energy phases, with each episode lasting at least two weeks, and with at least one episode of a low phase lasting at least two weeks in between, over the past year and a half, which could help differentiate between bipolar I and bipolar II disorder?

I'm really not sure about the exact timing or if my experiences fit into those specific alternating blocks. Mostly, I've just felt sped up and high-energy for the majority of the past year and a half, with only very brief periods of coming down or feeling flat.

Can you confirm if you have had any periods where you experienced at least four consecutive days of abnormally elevated mood, which were not followed by a period of at least two weeks of depressive symptoms, to help differentiate between the potential diagnoses?

Yes, my high-energy, revved-up phases last much longer than four days—in fact, they've been going on almost constantly for the past year and a half, only easing up briefly. I don't really experience long, two-week stretches of deep depression after these highs, but rather I just feel flat, low on energy, or slightly less keyed up than my usual high-energy self.
Can you describe any notable differences in the severity or impact of your high-energy phases versus your low phases on your daily life and relationships?

During my high-energy phases, I'm buzzing with activity, taking on way too much, and snapping at people, which has caused real trouble with my charting and classes at work. But when I hit those low phases, it's like all the life goes out of me; I'll just sit on the couch for hours, ignoring phone calls and completely pulling away from my family and friends.
